Every case's expected output was captured by running the unmodified bash hook directly against a staged throwaway CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR before being written here, never assumed (see the runner mechanisms added alongside this file: "setup_git"/"dirty_files" for git-backed nudge cases, "prime"/"files_after_prime" for the signature-gate cases, and "expect_context_excludes" — a new, symmetric-to-"expect_context" assertion — for the one discovery below that a positive substring match cannot rule out). This project's OWN progress.md convention — a bare backtick-wrapped line, e.g. this very work item's own .somi/plans/node-runtime-port/progress.md line 10, `` `in-progress` `` with no "Status:" prefix — matches NEITHER pattern, confirmed directly with grep -qiE against both regexes. So this hook, as currently written, would silently fail to surface node-runtime-port itself (or any other work item that follows this repo's own progress.md style) as an active work item on a fresh Claude Code turn. Meanwhile the R&D README.md convention (`> Status: `ready-for-planning`` — see examples/discovery-example.md:22) DOES match its sibling regex, because it already carries the "Status:" prefix the plans-detection regex additionally requires. This asymmetry is real, reproducible, and worth a naming call, not a silent default — filed below and in progress.md's Follow-ups as a decision for Phase 2 iteration 2.8 (the Node port of this hook) to make explicitly: normalize this repo's own progress.md convention to match the regex, or normalize the port's detection to match the convention actually in use. Note on the "files_after_prime" perturbation used in the signature-gate cases: it stages a brand-new .somi/reviews/*.md path (or a new file entirely) rather than touching an existing file's mtime, so the signature change is exact-listing-driven, not timing/mtime-resolution-dependent — deliberately avoids a flaky sleep-then-touch pattern. Note on ordering: the multi-in-progress case does not assert the specific slug list text, only the static surrounding phrase — verified directly that the slug order in that message follows `find`'s raw (unsorted) directory-traversal order, which is not stable across differently-created directories, so asserting an exact order would be a false, environment-fragile precision this fixture avoids. RESOLVED at Phase 2 iteration 2.8 (the Node port): chose to WIDEN the bare-line regex to accept backtick wrapping (full-line anchor preserved; empirically verified zero false positives against this repo's own progress.md narrative text) rather than reproduce the narrow bash detection for parity — see inject-workflow-context.mjs's header for the full reasoning and decisions.md's new D-entry. The `plan-hint-bare-backtick-status-not-detected` case below is renamed to `plan-hint-bare-backtick-status-now-detected` and its expectation flipped accordingly; every other case is unaffected (the R&D status regexes and the "status:"-prefixed in-progress regex had no discovered gap and are reproduced unchanged).

cases.name: prose-markdown-link-on-a-rejected-line-survives-untouched
cases._note:
NEW at pass 3 (F-37). Link flattening used to run on the WHOLE line before the recognizer, and both reject branches returned that flattened copy — so any line the recognizer DECLINED still had its markdown links destroyed. Measured: a bullet reading `read [the security file](./rules/30-security-owasp.md) before touching a sink` was injected as `read ./rules/30-security-owasp.md before touching a sink` — F19's exact output (a bare ENOENT path in a consuming project) reached through the opposite door, and via the `!citationMatch` branch, which has nothing to do with citations. The function's name and doc comment promised 'rewrites each line's trailing citation'; it in fact rewrote every markdown link on every line it touched, including lines it had explicitly decided not to handle.

WIDENED at pass 4: the first version staged only a prose-link bullet with no trailing parenthetical, which exercises just ONE of the function's three flattening paths — the `!citationMatch` early return. Measured: restoring the flattened-copy leak on the OTHER reject branch, and separately splicing the SUCCESS path's prefix from a flattened copy, each left all 134 fixtures green. Both reproduce F19's exact output (bare `./rules/NN-*.md` injected into Tier 2) and neither would have turned the suite red.

Three adjacent bullets now cover all three paths in one contiguous assertion: (1) prose link, NO parenthetical -> `!citationMatch` reject; (2) prose link + a REJECTED citation `(ISO 27001)` -> `!allItemsAreCitations` reject; (3) prose link + an ACCEPTED citation `` (`40`) `` -> success path, where the prefix must be spliced from the ORIGINAL line so the in-prose link survives while the citation rewrites. The assertion spans all three lines, so any of the three leaks turns this case red.

Note on an earlier overstatement: per-line (rather than block-level all-or-nothing) rejection is pinned by `plugin-root-env-resolves-and-strips-links`, not by this case — an earlier version of this note credited it here. Bullet (3) now makes the claim true of this case as well, since it proves an accepted and a rejected bullet coexist correctly in one block.

cases.name: non-citation-parenthetical-is-not-rewritten-as-a-rule-code
cases._note:
NEW at pass 2 (F-34). stripDigestCitations()'s recognizer previously scanned the line-final parenthetical UNANCHORED for any two-digit run, so any such parenthetical became a rule citation. Measured against a staged digest: a bullet ending `(ISO 27001)` was injected as `(`27`, `00`)` — a FABRICATED citation to two rule files, delivered into the model's context as fact. The function already had the right escape hatch (codes.length === 0 -> leave untouched); the recognizer was simply too loose to ever reach it.

Not hypothetical for this work item: phase 4 iteration 4.2 rewraps and trims this exact block, which is precisely when a non-citation parenthetical most plausibly lands at end-of-line.

The recognizer is now anchored — the whole parenthetical body must BE a comma-separated citation list (`NN` / bare NN / (./)rules/NN-*.md) or the line is returned untouched. `ISO 27001` fails because `27001` is not a two-digit item. Asserts the bullet survives VERBATIM and that no fabricated backticked code appears.
